messages:
carlos: Heads-up — noticed ~30% drop in tokens/sec on the canary after merge 4f1b9e7. CI perf job flagged it. Anyone already on a bisect?

alice: same here. Canary queueing times spiked, tail latency up. I grabbed a flamegraph.

alice: ```flamegraph snippet
kernel_select: +120ms
softmax_kernel: +10ms
memcpy: +45ms
queueing_delay: +80ms
```

dana: which commit changed scheduler/selection? run `git log -S'select_kernel' -p`?

bob: bisect in progress — narrowed to 4f1b9e7 -> 8c2a1d3. The change is in sched/heuristics.cc: we now prefer fast_attn_v2 when avg_seq>128, but that path does an extra GPU->CPU memcpy for small batches as a fallback.

emma: confirming locally: when batch_size<=4 and seq~64, tokens/sec goes down 28% with that kernel. Kernel switch has extra staging buffer.

carlos: can we gate it behind runtime flag + rollout? revert the heuristic for now.

dana: preparing revert PR now, testing on staging.

infra-bot: perf-ci: job tokens_per_sec dropped by 34% on step 42 for 4f1b9e7 -> 8c2a1d3, regression label PERFORMANCE.

alice: if revert is quick we can hold canary pause. patch should be small.

bob: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2593 reverting kernel-prefer heuristic. running canary job after merge.

emma: re-run canary now — staging looks closer to baseline, tokens/sec +27% versus canary with heuristic.

infra-bot: deploy: revert merged; canary scheduled for rollout at 2026-03-18T15:30:00Z.

carlos: thanks. action items: 1) add unit test for kernel path regression, 2) instrument memcpy counts in metric pipeline, 3) investigation: why fallback uses CPU staging.

dana: adding test and metric. will follow up PR with deeper fix.

alice: marking thread resolved after canary green :thumbsup:
